challenges.name: floating-promise-predict-quiz
challenges.title: Where did the error go?
challenges.description: Predict what happens to rejections that nobody awaits before you read on.

questions.explanation: forEach calls the async callback for each draft and throws away the promises it returns - it never waits for them. saveAll reaches toast("All drafts saved") synchronously, before any save has finished, and the try block is already left when the 409 arrives. That callback's promise rejects with no handler attached: the browser fires an unhandledrejection event (and logs "Uncaught (in promise)"), and Node.js would by default terminate the process. Use Promise.all(drafts.map(...)) and await it, so the error reaches the catch.

options.text: "Saving failed: HTTP 409" - the catch block receives the error from the callback.
"All drafts saved", shown before any save has finished; the 409 becomes an unhandled rejection.
"All drafts saved", shown after all saves finished; the 409 is silently ignored by forEach.
Nothing - forEach stops at the first rejected callback and saveAll never resumes.

questions.question: send() returns a promise that rejects after 100 ms. Which snippets end up reporting an unhandled rejection? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: void only discards the value - it attaches no handler. The DOM ignores whatever an event listener returns, so the promise returned by an async listener is never observed by anyone. A promise that rejects while you are still awaiting something else has no handler at that moment: the runtime reports it at the end of that task, and attaching the handler 2 seconds later only produces a rejectionhandled event afterwards. .catch() attaches a handler immediately, and Promise.all attaches handlers to every input, so the rejection is delivered to the await.

options.text: button.addEventListener("click", async () => { await send(); });  // then the button is clicked
const p = send(); await otherWork(); /* takes 2 s */ await p;

challenges.name: fix-fire-and-forget-checkout
challenges.title: Fix the fire-and-forget checkout
challenges.description: placeOrder() tracks analytics, prefetches the receipt template, creates the order and reserves stock. In production it floods error tracking with unhandled rejections, confirms orders whose reservations failed and leaves the spinner running after errors. Fix it so every promise has a handler from the moment it exists, the order waits for all reservations, optional work falls back instead of failing, and the spinner always stops. The tests run the checkout on a virtual clock and count every unhandled rejection the runtime reports.

tests.name: Happy path: the order is confirmed only after every reservation
Ad blocker: analytics rejects, the order goes through without an error report
Out of stock: the order fails and the spinner stops
Receipt template service down: confirm with the plain template
createOrder fails while analytics and the template fail too
